hook_text: A two-tonne car, a hand pump and a few millimetres per stroke. Then five hard questions about whether it is any good.
clip_script: A bottle jack is two cylinders with one-way doors. Pump up: oil in from the store. Pump down: oil forced into the big ram, which rises a few millimetres. The door shuts and holds it, because oil does not squash. Fifty to one, times a ten to one handle: 50 newtons lifts two and a half tonnes. Release valve, down it comes, slowly. Now judge it. Fitness: rated load, lift height, hard flat ground. Cost: a few hundred rand, lasts decades. Safety: it holds, but never go under a car on a jack alone; axle stand, chocks, handbrake. Aesthetics: clean finish and a stamped rating signal quality. Ergonomics: long handle, light pump force, gentle release, light to carry. Table it, with evidence.
visual_style: Whiteboard jack cross-section with oil arrows through two valves; a car rising; an axle stand sliding in; a five-row scorecard filling.
pacing: Pump, hold, release in fifteen seconds; five criteria at a clip.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the rated load stamped on a jack in a car boot.
